principles.title: Governance
principles.description: A bank's risk data aggregation capabilities and risk reporting practices should be subject to strong governance arrangements consistent with other principles and guidance established by the Committee.
principles.evidence: Model Risk Committee (MRC) established with formal Terms of Reference. Quarterly meeting cycle adopted. Tiering matrix (Materiality x Complexity) applied per Handbook Chapter 8. RAG ratings assigned to all models. Audit trail tracks all governance decisions with timestamps.
principles.gaps: Data governance policy not yet formalised as a standalone document. Board-level reporting on risk data quality not yet established.
principles.remediation: Draft standalone data governance policy. Establish quarterly board reporting on risk data quality metrics.

principles.title: Data Architecture and IT Infrastructure
principles.description: A bank should design, build and maintain data architecture and IT infrastructure which fully supports its risk data aggregation capabilities and risk reporting practices not only in normal times but also during times of stress or crisis.
principles.evidence: Centralised model architecture in src/models/ with clear separation of concerns. JSON data store with structured schemas (CDM layer). Model chain documented with field-level data handoffs between all 8 models. Configurable catchment-based data organisation.
principles.gaps: No formal data dictionary or metadata catalogue. Single-node architecture without high-availability or disaster recovery provisions.
principles.remediation: Create formal data dictionary covering all model inputs/outputs. Document data flow diagrams. Assess HA/DR requirements.

principles.title: Accuracy and Integrity
principles.description: A bank should be able to generate accurate and reliable risk data to meet normal and stress/crisis reporting accuracy requirements. Data should be aggregated on a largely automated basis so as to minimise the probability of errors.
principles.evidence: 518 automated tests (464 Python + 51 JavaScript) all passing. GEV statistical fitting with validated return periods. Depth-damage curves calibrated against EA data. Monte Carlo simulations with VaR/ES calculations. Automated parameter inventory tracking ~150+ parameters with source references.
principles.gaps: No formal data reconciliation process between model outputs. Limited stress testing of data aggregation under extreme scenarios.
principles.remediation: Implement automated reconciliation checks between model chain outputs. Design stress test scenarios for data aggregation pipeline.

principles.title: Completeness
principles.description: A bank should be able to capture and aggregate all material risk data across the bank. Data should be available by business line, legal entity, asset type, industry, region and other groupings that permit identifying and reporting risk exposures, concentrations and emerging risks.
principles.evidence: 8 models covering the complete risk chain: Storm Intensity, Storm-Gauge Response, GEV Hazard Curves, PRS Pricing, Depth-Damage, Property Valuation, Mortgage Pricer, Risk Assessor. Data aggregated by catchment, gauge, property, and mortgage portfolio dimensions. Property hazard curves link spatial flood risk to individual assets.
principles.gaps: Limited to physical flood risk; does not yet cover other risk types (market, credit, operational). Geographic coverage limited to configured catchments.
principles.remediation: Document scope limitations clearly. Assess extensibility to additional risk types and geographic regions.

principles.title: Timeliness
principles.description: A bank should be able to generate aggregate and up-to-date risk data in a timely manner while also meeting the principles relating to accuracy and integrity, completeness and adaptability.
principles.evidence: Batch portfolio generation with configurable parameters. On-demand report generation via CLI and dashboard. Historical daily gauge data processing pipeline.
principles.gaps: No real-time data feeds or streaming aggregation. No intraday risk reporting capability. Batch processing latency not formally measured or monitored.
principles.remediation: Establish SLAs for data aggregation timeliness. Implement processing time monitoring. Assess real-time data feed requirements.

principles.title: Adaptability
principles.description: A bank should be able to generate aggregate risk data to meet a broad range of on-demand, ad hoc risk management reporting requests, including requests during stress/crisis situations.
principles.evidence: Configurable catchment system allows adding new geographic areas. Modular generator architecture (src/port/src/) enables new data products. Interactive dashboard supports ad-hoc queries with drill-down. CLI subcommands (server, port, visual, check, config) provide flexible execution modes.
principles.gaps: No formal stress scenario framework for ad-hoc reporting. Limited ability to rapidly reconfigure model parameters under crisis conditions.
principles.remediation: Design pre-defined stress scenarios with rapid activation capability. Document ad-hoc reporting procedures.

principles.title: Accuracy (Reporting)
principles.description: Risk management reports should accurately and precisely convey aggregated risk data and reflect risk in an exact manner. Reports should be reconciled and validated.
principles.evidence: Automated PDF generation for meeting packs, parameter inventories, test results, and model documentation. ReportLab-based report generation with structured tables and formatted output. LaTeX document generation for formal governance documents (ToR, parameter inventory, test reports).
principles.gaps: No formal report validation or sign-off process. No automated reconciliation between dashboard displays and PDF reports.
principles.remediation: Implement report validation checksums. Establish formal report sign-off workflow in MRC process.

principles.title: Comprehensiveness
principles.description: Risk management reports should cover all material risk areas within the organisation. The depth and scope of these reports should be consistent with the size and complexity of the bank's operations and risk profile.
principles.evidence: Risk reporting covers flood hazard, property damage, mortgage credit risk, insurance pricing, and portfolio risk dimensions. Model chain provides end-to-end coverage from natural hazard through to financial impact. VaR, Expected Shortfall, and HHI concentration metrics calculated.
principles.gaps: Reporting scope limited to physical flood risk vertical. No cross-risk aggregation with other risk types.
principles.remediation: Document reporting scope and materiality assessment. Plan for extension to additional risk dimensions as platform grows.

principles.title: Clarity and Usefulness
principles.description: Risk management reports should communicate information in a clear and concise manner. Reports should be easy to understand yet comprehensive enough to facilitate informed decision-making.
principles.evidence: Interactive Leaflet map dashboard with colour-coded markers, tooltips, and context menus. Tabbed governance panel with inventory, model chain visualisation, and MRC management. PDF meeting packs with structured agenda, minutes, decisions, and actions. Notification system for user feedback.
principles.gaps: No formal user feedback mechanism for report usefulness. Dashboard does not include executive summary views.
principles.remediation: Add executive summary dashboard view. Implement user satisfaction tracking for reports.

principles.title: Frequency
principles.description: The board should set the frequency of risk management report production and distribution. Frequency requirements should reflect the needs of the recipients.
principles.evidence: Quarterly MRC meeting cycle established. Reports generated on demand via CLI and dashboard. Test results can be regenerated at any time.
principles.gaps: No automated scheduled report generation. No formal frequency policy for different report types. No monitoring of report distribution timeliness.
principles.remediation: Establish formal report frequency policy. Implement scheduled report generation capability. Track report distribution and acknowledgement.

principles.title: Distribution
principles.description: Risk management reports should be distributed to the relevant parties while ensuring confidentiality.
principles.evidence: PDF export capability for all governance documents. Meeting document upload and download functionality. Dashboard accessible via web browser. Documents marked CONFIDENTIAL in LaTeX headers.
principles.gaps: No role-based access controls on dashboard or documents. No formal distribution list management. No audit trail of document access.
principles.remediation: Implement role-based access controls. Create formal distribution lists for report types. Add document access logging.

principles.title: Review
principles.description: Supervisors should periodically review and evaluate a bank's compliance with the eleven Principles.
principles.evidence: MRC quarterly review cycle with documented agenda, minutes, decisions, and actions. Audit trail captures all governance changes with timestamps. RAG ratings reviewed at each MRC meeting. Model validation status tracked in inventory.
principles.gaps: No independent external review of BCBS 239 compliance. Self-assessment not yet formalised as a regular process.
principles.remediation: Formalise BCBS 239 self-assessment as annual MRC agenda item. Consider commissioning independent compliance review.

principles.title: Remedial Actions and Supervisory Measures
principles.description: Supervisors should have and use the appropriate tools and resources to require effective and timely remedial action by a bank to address deficiencies in its risk data aggregation capabilities and risk reporting practices.
principles.evidence: MRC action tracking with owners, target dates, and status (Open/In Progress/Closed). Decisions formally recorded with IDs and dates. Remediation priorities agreed at inaugural MRC meeting with 5 specific actions.
principles.gaps: No escalation workflow for overdue actions. No automated alerts for approaching deadlines.
principles.remediation: Implement overdue action alerting. Define escalation procedures for missed remediation deadlines.

principles.title: Home/Host Cooperation
principles.description: Supervisors should cooperate with relevant supervisors in other jurisdictions regarding the supervision and review of the Principles, and the implementation of any remedial action if necessary.
principles.evidence: Single-jurisdiction operation currently. Governance framework designed to be extensible to multi-jurisdictional requirements.
principles.gaps: No cross-jurisdictional supervisory coordination framework. Not yet applicable given current single-jurisdiction scope.
principles.remediation: Document jurisdictional scope. Prepare framework for multi-jurisdictional coordination when required.
